findings.finding: gpu/backends/gpu.py _CELL_GATES is a module-global in-RAM dict with a PUBLIC writer: any in-process caller may call cell_gate(passed=True, ...) and open a cell. 'Only the device-side harness can open a cell' is a procedure, not an enforced invariant. Additionally the docstring 'CPU-only callers must never pass passed=True' is contradicted by two legitimate in-RAM test fixtures. In THIS build no harm is reachable (terminal step-4 raise); the exposure becomes real the moment G11 wires a context port.
findings.requested_disposition: G11: make the durable evidence-backed store authoritative for cell_is_gated_open (read recorded evidence, not in-RAM writable state) before any device dispatch exists; fix the docstring to describe the actual contract

findings.finding: kept_prefix (gpu/kernels/host_twins.py) docstring claims it 'Validates finiteness of the kept values' but the body only checks length mismatch — no finiteness check exists. No behavior defect (post-K0 finite-domain reliance is separately recorded), but the docstring asserts validation that does not happen.
findings.requested_disposition: implement the finiteness check or reword the docstring in a follow-up implementation change

findings.finding: validate_device_bits main() returns EXIT_PASSED (0) for --emit-host-battery, overloading the documented '0 = gate PASSED on a real device'. A script keying on rc==0 alone would read a host-only battery emission as gate-passed. Mitigated: stdout says 'host_battery_written ... device half requires real hardware and stays unrun' and no path marks a cell bit_validated.
findings.requested_disposition: distinct exit code (e.g. 5) for the host-battery mode before G11 automation consumes rc

findings.finding: run_host_stage_composition constructs FoldCell(bit_validated=True). Verified functionally inert (validate_request never reads request.cell; the ladder consults the store), and the helper is marked gate/tests-only with a non-dispatching record — but the forged flag invites exactly the misreading the fail-closed law warns about.
findings.requested_disposition: optional inline comment naming the flag's inertness; no behavior change
